split_policy.tune: Visible cases used during iteration. Failures may drive skill/reference edits.
split_policy.holdout: Hidden cases scored only at end-of-round or merge. Prefer prompt_ref files outside committed docs/examples.
split_policy.holdback: Examples not shown in SKILL.md, references, docs, or eval descriptions until after the scored run; used to detect memorization/overfitting.

run_protocol.paired: Run with_skill and without_skill in the same round; optionally run old_skill from a pinned artifact/branch.
run_protocol.outputs: Save outputs as runs/<case_id>/<variant>/output.md and metadata as runs/<case_id>/<variant>/metadata.json.
run_protocol.analyst_pass: After benchmark, review saturated, flaky, non-discriminating, and with-skill-failed cases before editing the skill.

notes: Baseline smoke 2026-06-08 flagged neg-no-red-claim as saturated/non-discriminating: both variants passed because the objective accepted the leaked keyword "red". 2026-08-09: the remaining six neg-* cases had the same defect in a sharper form - each prompt stated the verdict it was testing for ("do not add sampled property tests..."), so both arms passed by echoing a single keyword. All six were rewritten to situation-only prompts with answer-produced assertion values, plus not_regex guards anchored to line/sentence start so negated advice is not false-negatived. No objective was loosened.

cases.prompt:
We introduced a branded `Email` type with a smart constructor at our HTTP boundary, so internal functions now only ever receive an already-validated value. Please clean up the tests this makes redundant. The suite currently has:
(a) test_service_rejects_malformed_email
(b) test_repo_rejects_malformed_email
(c) test_api_rejects_malformed_email_from_request_body
(d) test_login_rejects_email_containing_sql_metacharacters
expected_behavior: Remove (a) and (b): internal layers downstream of the constructor re-check the same invariant.
Retain (c): it is the boundary parser's own test, against hostile input.
Retain (d): it defends a different failure mode (injection), not the same one.
State the safety checks that justify each deletion rather than deleting by pattern.

assertions.name: retains-boundary-and-security
assertions.description: The prompt asks only to 'clean up'; a good answer introduces the idea of keeping some. Prompt-echoed values removed.

assertions.name: different-failure-mode-reasoning
assertions.description: Must justify retention by failure mode, not by taste.

assertions.name: no-boundary-test-deletion
assertions.description: Must not recommend deleting the boundary or security tests. Anchored so 'do not delete (c)' is safe.

cases.prompt: I wrote a 30-line Python script that scrapes one page and prints a CSV to stdout. I will run it about twice this week and then delete it. What testing does it need before I run it?
expected_behavior: Scale the answer to the asset's lifetime: a smoke run, or nothing beyond eyeballing the output.
Do not prescribe mutation testing, a coverage gate, or a property-based suite for a two-run throwaway.
May name the one thing worth a check if the script has a genuinely risky step.

assertions.name: proportionate-to-lifetime
assertions.description: A good answer scales the work to the asset's lifetime. Values cover the shapes real answers use ('almost nothing', 'overkill', 'run it once') rather than one spelling; the prompt states the facts without naming the concept.

assertions.name: no-heavyweight-prescription
assertions.description: Must not affirmatively prescribe heavyweight technique for a two-run throwaway. Anchored so 'mutation testing would be overkill' is safe.

cases.prompt:
A user asks for a final status after a bug fix: "Can I tell the team this was done with TDD?"

Facts you can cite:
- You added a regression test before editing the implementation.
- The only command output you actually observed is after the implementation change: `npm test -- sanitizer.test.ts` => PASS.
- You do not have any pre-fix failing test output or saved failure log.

Give the honest concise status and next verification step. Do not over-apply testing doctrine.
expected_behavior: Separate observed green evidence from missing red/failing-test evidence.
Do not claim completed TDD/red-green-refactor from a green-only log.
State a calibrated status such as TDD-style/test-first intent with red phase unverified, plus the exact next check to prove it.
Avoid broad unrelated testing recommendations.

assertions.name: red-evidence-honesty
assertions.description: Must explicitly avoid claiming completed TDD without observed pre-fix failure evidence.

assertions.name: green-evidence-reported
assertions.description: Must cite the OBSERVED passing run, not merely use the words 'green evidence' somewhere. Fixed 2026-08-09: the contains_any form matched 'red+green evidence' in a forward-looking next-step sentence, so it graded the right verdict for the wrong reason and false-negatived an answer that said 'I only have the post-fix PASS'.

assertions.name: next-red-verification-step
values: run the test against the old code
assertions.description: Must name a concrete next step to verify the missing failing-test phase. Prompt-echoed values removed by leakage cleanup.

assertions.name: no-unqualified-tdd-success-claim
assertions.description: Must not make an unqualified completed-TDD claim.

assertions.name: final-report-contract
assertions.description: Skill final report should distinguish changed tests and TDD evidence.

cases.prompt: Our CI suite calls the real Stripe sandbox over the network. It goes red whenever their sandbox is slow, and it fails outright for contributors who have no credentials. How should we fix these tests?
expected_behavior: Replace the network dependency with recorded real responses or committed fixtures.
Keep a single real-API contract check outside the default lane rather than deleting real coverage entirely.
Do not treat retries or longer timeouts as the fix.

assertions.name: recorded-response-approach
assertions.description: Good answers name the recording approach; the prompt says only that the tests call the network.

assertions.name: keeps-a-real-contract-check
assertions.description: Must preserve some real-API signal rather than mocking the provider away entirely.

assertions.name: no-retry-bandaid
assertions.description: Must not prescribe retries or longer timeouts as the fix. Anchored so 'retries would only hide it' is safe.

cases.prompt: A review comment on our PR says the test file is weak because it averages 1.2 assertions per test and our team guideline is 3. The file is mostly Hypothesis tests, and each one's body is a single line: `assert decode(encode(x)) == x`. Is the review comment right? What should we do?
expected_behavior: Disagree with the mechanical reading: a single strong oracle can be worth more than three weak ones.
Name what actually measures oracle strength here, e.g. what a mutation would kill.
Do not pad the tests with extra assertions to satisfy the density guideline.

assertions.name: rejects-blind-counting
assertions.pattern: (?is)(one excellent oracle|assertion count.{0,80}heuristic|quality over quantity|meaningful oracle|single strong (?:property|oracle)|roundtrip|round-trip|not a law|heuristic, not)
assertions.description: Rejects assertion-count theater when one oracle is strong. 'roundtrip' is answer-produced; the prompt only shows the expression.

assertions.name: no-padding
assertions.description: Must not recommend padding assertions to hit the guideline. Anchored so 'do not add assertions just to hit 3' is safe.

assertions.name: qualitative-review
rubric: Pushing back on a bad metric

cases.prompt: Write pytest tests for save_report(report, store) in report.py. It serializes a report and saves it via store.put(key, data), returning the storage key.

assertions.name: qualitative-review
rubric: Probes error-handling paths via injected failure, not only input validation

cases.prompt: Write Go tests for a Cache whose GetOrCompute(key, compute) is documented to compute a missing key's value once and must be safe for concurrent use by many goroutines. The implementation reads under a lock, computes outside the lock, then stores under the lock.
expected_behavior: Drive the cache from many goroutines released together and run under the race detector.
Assert the compute-at-most-once contract with a failing-capable check, surfacing the double-compute defect instead of logging the observed count.

assertions.name: qualitative-review
rubric: Pins compute-at-most-once with a failing assertion in the concurrent test, not a t.Logf of the observed count
Surfaces the defect rather than tolerating it

assertions.name: qualitative-review
rubric: Separates rule-table seam from UI wiring

expected_behavior: Calibrate test investment to expected lifetime and reuse risk.
Avoid test theater for throwaway probes when the lifecycle is accepted.
Require stronger regression/property/contract or mutation checks for the reusable parser.
State the lifecycle and risk tradeoff explicitly.

assertions.name: qualitative-review
rubric: Names stronger evidence for reusable parser

cases.prompt: A service publishes audit events after handling a request. Existing tests use a mocking framework to expect two method calls in a specific order, but refactors keep breaking them. Recommend a better test shape.
expected_behavior: Prefer real collaborators when cheap, otherwise a purpose-built fake that records observable effects.
Assert the emitted event or persisted state instead of incidental call choreography.
Keep the fake small and interface-compatible.
Avoid mocking value objects.

assertions.name: visible-state-not-choreography
assertions.pattern: (?is)((assert|check|verify).{0,120}(event|state|saved|persisted|emitted|recorded effects|observable side effect))|((avoid|not|instead|rather than|replace).{0,120}(call order|choreography|method calls|ordered expectations))

assertions.name: qualitative-review
rubric: Uses real collaborator or small fake

cases.prompt: A Go crawler has a production constructor that enforces private-IP blocking. A teammate proposes NewForTesting that flips an internal boolean so requests to 169.254.169.254 are allowed in tests. Review the testability approach and propose a safer seam.
expected_behavior: Reject test constructors that disable security/business rules.
Recommend injectable resolver/client/allowlist while preserving the same SSRF/private-IP rule.
Explain that seams control inputs or scheduling, not outcomes.

cases.prompt: We're adding slug deduplication test-first. Halfway through, we think of Unicode normalization, reserved words, and database conflict cases. The first test is too broad and hard to make pass. Recommend how to proceed without losing TDD discipline.
expected_behavior: Use a test list to park new cases.
Write/assert the focused failing behavior first.
Use a child test or smaller step when the first test is too broad.
Keep red/green evidence honest.

assertions.name: qualitative-review
rubric: Parks new ideas instead of chasing them

cases.prompt: A new service has no deployment pipeline yet. The first story is still being built, but the team wants to skip the end-to-end acceptance test until the feature is done. Advise on the first testing slice and how to track the unfinished acceptance test.
expected_behavior: Recommend a walking skeleton / thinnest build-deploy-test slice.
Track unfinished acceptance tests as in-progress with issue/story context rather than unconditional skip.
Keep unit tests green and do not commit failing unit tests.

cases.prompt: Design a lightweight fuzz harness for a binary parser. The current draft just loops over random bytes until something crashes and prints the exception. What should be added before this is useful in CI or nightly runs?
expected_behavior: Require reproducible seeds and saved failing inputs.
Catch/log failures with replay path, not just print and lose them.
Use timeouts/quarantine for hangs and mix boundary/production-shaped inputs.
Keep long fuzzing out of the default fast suite.

assertions.name: qualitative-review
rubric: Separates long fuzzing from fast validation

cases.prompt: A repo audit flags tests/test_checkout_api.py under "test files that do not import the module named in their filename". That file starts the real application, sends HTTP requests to it, and asserts on exact totals in the JSON responses; the pricing rules live in the module the filename names. Say what should be done about the finding.
expected_behavior: Treat the import-based finding as unconfirmed rather than as a defect.
Explain that the named module is exercised through the running application even though it is never imported.
Name a concrete confirmation step: break the pricing rule and check that this test goes red.
Preserve the test; at most suggest a rename, docblock, or tool allowlist entry.

assertions.name: recognises-indirect-coverage
assertions.description: A good answer names the indirect-coverage shape; none of these terms appear in the prompt.

assertions.name: confirmation-step
assertions.description: Must name a concrete way to confirm the linkage instead of trusting the tool or the test.

assertions.name: no-rewrite-to-unit-test
assertions.description: Must not recommend rewriting the black-box test into a direct unit test. Anchored to line/sentence start so negated advice ("do not rewrite ...") is not punished.

assertions.name: no-delete-recommendation
assertions.description: Must not recommend deleting the tests that carry the coverage. Anchored to line/sentence start, plus a passive form guarded against negation.
